surfaces.part: cobblestone ground texture, full tile of irregular dark purple stones separated by dark mortar lines

answer.evidence: This is a seamless terrain tile of Voronoi-like cobblestones seen from above, filling the whole 112x80 area. There is no standing object, no silhouette, no front face and no eave or edge line separating a top from a south face. The column scans show only alternating stone and mortar bands (dark #0e0a14 lines) with no consistent edge-line-plus-shadow structure. It reads as a flat ground texture, which is appropriate for the terrain kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a dark purple flagstone patch, so the paving reference is the right comparison. Its grout lines are tinted dark purple, not neutral black, which matches the 23% near-neutral share of dark edge pixels. That is the Beodeul approach, and the stones are separated by value rather than a sticker outline. Shading is the weak point. The whole patch uses only 10 distinct colours and about 4 lightness steps, against roughly 6 on the paving reference. Each stone is a mostly smooth fill with a faint horizontal streak and a thin lit edge. The paving reference has gritty speckle inside each stone and clear per-stone highlights. The candidate has 5 visible tones per tile against 7 for the paving reference, and 8% near-flat coverage against 0%. It beats the grass reference on tones (3), but paving is the closer kind, so I judge against that. It reads as clean and coherent but visibly thinner and flatter than the paving reference. A few isolated sparkle dots do not make up for the missing per-stone grain, so it fails on a cautious call.
